seance.1.but: Know where you are, see what is there, move around and come back home.
seance.1.question: What does the computer answer to pwd? Why does the path start with / ?
seance.1.bloque: Are you looking for where you are, or what is here?
seance.1.piege: the forgotten space (cd.. instead of cd ..)
seance.1.fini: ls -a in the home folder: what are these files starting with a dot?
seance.1.p3: Where am I? · The old path
seance.1.trace: A computer keeps its files in folders, like the branches of a tree; the trunk is called the root `/`.
`pwd` tells where I am, `ls` shows what is here.
`cd place` moves me, `cd ~` brings me home.
seance.2.but: Create a folder and a file, write in it, read it, see hidden files.
seance.2.question: What happens if you use > twice? How do you see a hidden file?
seance.2.bloque: Do you want to create a folder, or write in a file?
seance.2.piege: > replaces all the content; rm deletes with no bin
seance.2.p2: Build my nest · One place too many
seance.2.trace: `mkdir` creates a folder, `touch` creates an empty file.
`echo text > file` writes in a file (and replaces what was there), `cat file` reads it.
A name starting with a dot is hidden: `ls -a` shows it. `rm` deletes with no bin.
seance.3.but: See a whole tree, move, rename, copy and delete.
seance.3.question: mv does two things: which ones?
seance.3.bloque: Do you want to keep the original (copy) or move it?
seance.3.fini: cp -r of a whole folder, then ls -R to check
seance.3.trace: `cp source copy` copies (`cp -r` for a folder). `rm` deletes.
seance.4.but: Know who you are for the computer, read and change a file's permissions.
seance.4.question: What does rw-r--r-- mean in plain words?
seance.4.bloque: Who may read? Who may write?
seance.4.piege: after chmod 444, writing is refused: that's on purpose
seance.4.fini: read ls -l and say the permissions in words
seance.4.trace: Each file has an owner and permissions: read `r`, write `w`, run `x`.
`/etc`, `/bin` and `/var/log` belong to the system: look, don't touch.
seance.5.but: Find the lost book somewhere in the library.
seance.5.question: What is the difference between find and grep?
seance.5.bloque: Its name has the word book… but where is it kept? Are you looking for a FILE or a WORD?
seance.5.piege: you leave less with the q key; quotes around *livre*
seance.5.fini: grep -rn Abyssor . | wc -l: how many times does the name appear?
seance.5.trace: `find . -name "*word*"` looks for FILES by their name.
`grep word file` looks for a WORD in a text.
The pipe `|` gives one command's result to the next.
seance.6.but: Measure memory and disk, find what takes up space.
seance.6.question: RAM or disk: which one keeps files when you switch off?
seance.6.bloque: Are you measuring memory (free) or disk (df, du)?
seance.6.fini: du -sh * to find what weighs most
seance.6.trace: RAM is used while the computer works (`free -h`), the disk keeps the files (`df -h`).
`du -sh` tells how much a folder weighs.
Kilo, mega, giga: each unit is about a thousand times the one before.
seance.7.but: See running programs, start one in the background, stop it.
seance.7.question: What is the & at the end of a command for?
seance.7.bloque: Do you want to see programs (ps, jobs) or stop one (kill)?
seance.7.piege: kill stops a program, it doesn't “kill” anything
seance.7.fini: start two sleep … & and stop only one
seance.7.trace: A running program is called a process: `ps aux` lists them.
With `&`, a command works in the background while you keep typing.
`jobs` lists my tasks, `kill %1` stops the first one.
seance.8.but: Write and run a small script, keep your work's history with git.
seance.8.question: What is a commit, in one sentence?
seance.8.bloque: Is your script allowed to run?
seance.8.fini: a second recipe, then git diff between them
seance.8.trace: A script is a file full of commands: `sh script.sh` runs them.
An alias gives a command a short name.
git keeps successive snapshots of a work (commits): `git diff` shows what changed, `git log` the history.
seance.9.but: Test a connection, see your address, understand a site's name.
seance.9.question: Why do we need a directory (DNS) to reach a site?
seance.9.bloque: Do you want to know if a machine answers, or what its address is?
seance.9.piege: the school filter sometimes blocks ping (use world 11, simulated network)
seance.9.fini: nslookup on three sites: do their addresses look alike?
seance.9.trace: Each machine on the network has an IP address (`ip a`).
`ping` checks that a machine answers, `curl` asks for a web page.
`nslookup` turns a name into an address: it's the Internet's directory (DNS).
seance.10.but: Solve three trials without being given the commands: choose the tool for the problem.
seance.10.question: Which command did you use, and why that one?
seance.10.bloque: Which sheet talks about searching? Reading? Protecting?
seance.10.piege: give no command: point to the written summaries
seance.10.fini: invent a fourth trial for another pair
seance.10.trace: To solve a problem in the terminal: observe (`ls -a`, `cat`), search (`find`, `grep`), combine (`|`, `>`), protect (`chmod`).
The terminal is a toolbox: choose the tool for the problem.

reveil.gardien.1.texte: Before the great sleep, Ricanombre knew every room in the Terminaworld, even the hidden rooms whose names start with a dot. He laughed all the time, so that visitors were never afraid of getting lost. One day, commands became rarer and rarer, and the world began to doze off. So Ricanombre hid the rooms one by one, so that nothing would be lost during the night. He even hid his own room, and he fell asleep inside it.
reveil.gardien.2.texte: Heaumbre decided who could read, write or enter each chest. When the world fell asleep, he was afraid that someone would damage what was left. He closed all the padlocks, everywhere, very tight. Nobody could break anything any more… but nobody could get in either! Since then, he has understood that a good padlock lets the right people through.
reveil.gardien.3.texte: Cranard kept the passwords of the doors of the Terminaworld. So as not to forget them, he had written them all in a little notebook. But a secret written in a file is not really a secret any more: anyone can read it! Before falling asleep, he hid the notebook at the very bottom of a box. That is why, in his box, you search for forgotten secrets.
reveil.gardien.4.titre: Ombrachne, the guardian of the hangar
reveil.gardien.4.texte: Ombrachne wove threads between all the crates of the great hangar, so that everything stayed in its place. She was the one who noticed the first sign: threads that broke, messages that no longer arrived from one biome to another. She wanted to repair everything alone, thread after thread. But she was so tired that she fell asleep in the middle of her web.
reveil.gardien.5.texte: Marionnoire taught machines to repeat tasks all by themselves, like well-tuned puppets. During the great sleep, his scripts kept running, again and again, with nobody watching them. He understood something important: a machine needs someone to check what it is doing. He is waiting for a child to come and read his scripts again.
reveil.gardien.6.texte: Torsillon kept the old coded messages of the Terminaworld. One evening, he decoded a very old one, written by the first inhabitants. It said: “When nobody types any more, the world will sleep. And it will wake up command by command.” Torsillon kept this message like a treasure, waiting for the first command.
reveil.gardien.7.texte: Osselet can read the traces left by each command, like a detective. While searching the last traces from before the sleep, he found something surprising: an egg laid in a nest, at base camp, and a little green glow that would not go out. He understood that someone would come back. He wrote all of it in his journal, so as not to forget.
reveil.gardien.8.titre: Drapouille, the guardian of the nest
reveil.gardien.8.texte: Drapouille knows every trick: fake messages, trapped links, strangers who are too nice. During the great sleep, he watched over the nest, so that nobody could fool the egg. When your creature came out of its shell, he smiled under his sheet. He says all the guardians will meet again at the Heart, on the day the Terminaworld is completely awake.
qu.tresor.dit: ★ A secret treasure! You found it with find, like a real explorer.
qu.m01.texte: 🌋 Behind the lava flow, a small warm room! The blacksmiths keep their oldest hammers here. It smells of iron and toast.
qu.m02.texte: ⚓ An old shipwreck, hidden at the bottom of the Port! Shells have grown on the hull, and a little crab waves hello.
qu.m03.texte: ❄ A frost cave under the ice palace! The walls shine like thousands of little mirrors.
qu.m04.texte: 💧 Behind the Guild's waterfall, a secret cave! The water makes a curtain, and you can hear the drops singing.
qu.m05.texte: ⛰ A little shelter at the very top of the peak! There is a blanket, a lamp and a notebook where climbers draw the view.
qu.m06.texte: 🛡 A secret passage in the ramparts of the Citadel! The sentinels use it to do their rounds without getting wet.
qu.m07.texte: ⚡ The fuse room of the Control Post! Hundreds of little lights blink in rhythm, like a song.
qu.m08.texte: 🔧 The Workshop's parts cupboard! Screws, springs, bolts… and a little robot taking a nap.
qu.m09.texte: 📡 A nest at the very top of the Tower of Waves! Messages rest here before flying off into the sky again.
qu.m10.texte: 🌳 A burrow between the roots of the great tree! The rings of the wood tell the whole story of the Terminaworld.
qu.m11.texte: 🔭 A telescope hidden under the Observatory's dome! It looks at a star that nobody has named yet.
qu.m12.texte: ⚙ A secret gear behind the big wheel! It turns very slowly and goes tick, tock, tick, tock.
qu.m13.texte: 🕯 A forgotten vault in the Crypt of Codes! On the wall, jumbled letters are waiting to be decoded.
qu.m14.texte: ★🗺 A treasure map drawn by the builders of the Guild! You found it with `find`: well done, explorer.
qu.m15.texte: ★🗝 A wooden key, hidden deep in the roots! Nobody knows yet what it opens. You found it with `find`.
qu.m16.texte: 🐾 Hi, it's Braisillon! My forge is a real mess. Will you make me an enclume folder (an anvil), here in the Forge? (`mkdir enclume`)
qu.m17.texte: 🐾 I'm Fondelin, the apprentice blacksmith. I need three ingots on the anvil: lingot_1.txt, lingot_2.txt and lingot_3.txt in forge/enclume/. Example: `echo gold > enclume/lingot_1.txt`
qu.m18.texte: 🐾 Oh no! It's Plouftin, the Port's sailor. The storm scattered my 3 bottles, even into hidden corners. Find them (`find . -name "bouteille*"`), then put them all in a filet folder (a net) (`mkdir filet`, then `mv`).
qu.m19.texte: 🐾 Hello, I'm Tritonnet! The lighthouse needs a message for the boats. Write one in message.txt, here at the Port: `echo "all is well" > message.txt`
qu.m20.texte: 🐾 Brrr, it's Givrichon! My snowflakes are all mixed up in flocons.txt. Put them in order, in a new file: `sort flocons.txt > flocons_ranges.txt`
qu.m21.texte: 🐾 I'm Givrarde. How many ice cubes are there in glacons.txt? Count the lines with `wc -l glacons.txt`, then write just the number in reponse_glacons.txt.
qu.m22.texte: 🐾 Hi, it's Racinelle! Will you help me build a hut (cabane) with a roof (toit)? A cabane folder, and inside it a toit folder: `mkdir -p cabane/toit`
qu.m23.texte: 🐾 I'm Petalouette! I have 4 seeds in the graines folder. Will you copy them all into a jardin folder (a garden) so I can plant them? `cp -r graines jardin`
qu.m24.texte: 🐾 Hey, it's Cailloute! Up here, climbers leave a word in registre.txt. Write your creature's name (not your real name): `echo Noisette > registre.txt`
qu.m25.texte: 🐾 I'm Auréolin. How many pebbles are there in the tas folder? Look with `ls tas`, then write just the number in reponse_cailloux.txt.
qu.m26.texte: 🐾 Psst… it's Lanternix. My journal_de_lanternix.txt is precious. Will you put a padlock on it so nobody can damage it? (`chmod 444 journal_de_lanternix.txt`)
qu.m27.texte: 🐾 I'm Papillombre. I lost some scales from my wings in the night garden. Will you look for them for me? `find . -name "*.aile"`
qu.m28.texte: 🐾 Beep beep, it's Boulonnet! What time is it for the machines? Ask the computer: `date`
qu.m29.texte: 🐾 I'm Engrenaille. I need the inventory of the Control Post. Put the list of what is here into a file: `ls > inventaire.txt`
qu.m30.texte: 🐾 Creak, creak… it's Rouillot! I'm building a robot, but it has no name. Will you write one in robot.txt? `echo Beep > robot.txt`
qu.m31.texte: 🐾 I'm Parasouris. My 5 screws are lying around in the pieces folder. Will you copy them into a boite folder (a box)? `mkdir boite`, then `cp pieces/vis_* boite`
qu.m32.texte: 🐾 Bzzt, it's Zapiot! Send a little hello to the Terminaworld, it will answer you: `ping -c 1 127.0.0.1`
qu.m33.texte: 🐾 I'm Plumange. Write a word in the sky, I will carry it up to the clouds: `echo hello > ciel.txt`
qu.m34.texte: 🐾 Tick tock, it's Horlogrif! My clocks have no home. Will you make them a horloges folder in the Library? `mkdir horloges`
qu.m35.texte: 🐾 I'm Lunacorne. In the Library of Time, we write down every day. Write today's date in jour.txt: `date > jour.txt`
qu.m36.texte: 🐾 Hi, it's Miroeil! I drew the map of the sky. Will you look at it with me? `cat carte_du_ciel.txt`
qu.m37.texte: 🐾 I'm Nébuline. How many stars are there in etoiles.txt? Count the lines with `wc -l etoiles.txt`, then write just the number in reponse_etoiles.txt.
qu.m38.texte: 🐾 Boing! It's Ressortine. The big wheel needs a part: create a file roue.txt here. (`touch roue.txt`, or `echo wheel > roue.txt`)
qu.m39.texte: 🐾 I'm Scintipède. How many teeth are there in the engrenages folder? Look with `ls engrenages`, then write just the number in reponse_dents.txt.
qu.m40.texte: 🐾 Caw, it's Corbouh! My scroll is very long. Read only the first two lines: `head -n 2 parchemin_de_corbouh.txt`
qu.m41.texte: 🐾 I'm Araignoir. A secret word is caught in my toile.txt (my web). Find it (`grep MOTSECRET toile.txt`) and write it in mot_de_la_toile.txt.

cr.indice.plus_tard: OK, later! {nom} puts its wish away.
cr.gouts.aucun: {nom} comes from before the bestiary: its tastes are a mystery.
cr.gouts.secret: A secret taste: ? ? ? (try commands: it will tell you when you find it)
cr.gouts.pied: Its favourite dish and its secret taste count double for hunger (no extra XP). No command is disliked.
cr.album.oeuf: Still in its egg: the album starts when it hatches.
cr.album.pied: Stages to come stay as silhouettes. `tg album <name>`: the album of a creature in your team.
cr.album.pied.tel: Stages to come stay as silhouettes. `album <name>`: the album of a creature in your team.
cr.album.inconnu: Nobody is called “{nom}” in your team.
cr.album.toucher: Tap a stage: it waves at you. Tap outside to close.
cr.aide: `tg album` the album of its stages · `tg gouts` what it likes · `tg indice` a hint for its mystery wish
cr.aide.tel: 📖 Album: `album` (its stages) · `gouts` (what it likes) · `indice` (a hint for its mystery wish)
cr.dev.ls_a.d: A command that shows ALL the files, even the ones that hide!
cr.dev.ls_a.i1: It starts like the command that lists files.
cr.dev.ls_a.i2: It's `ls` with a small option: a dash and a letter…
cr.dev.pwd.d: A command that tells where I am, right now, in the world.
cr.dev.pwd.i2: It starts with “p” and ends with “d”.
cr.dev.ls.d: A command that shows what's in the place where we are.
cr.dev.ls.i1: It's one of the very first ones you learned.
cr.dev.ls.i2: Two letters: the first one is “l”.
cr.dev.whoami.d: A command that answers the question “who am I?”.
cr.dev.whoami.i1: It's that very question, written as one word.
cr.dev.date.d: A command that tells what day it is, and the time.
cr.dev.date.i1: It's the English word for the day on the calendar.
cr.dev.mkdir.d: A command that builds a new room (a folder).
cr.dev.cat.d: A command that shows what is written in a file.
cr.dev.cat.i1: Its name is an animal that meows.
cr.dev.cat.i2: Three letters: “c”, “a”, “t”… then the file name.
cr.dev.grep.d: A command that looks for a word in a file.
cr.dev.grep.i1: It's very useful after a pipe `|`.
cr.dev.ls_l.d: A command that shows files with all their details (size, date, permissions).
cr.dev.ls_l.i1: It's the listing command, with an option.
cr.dev.ls_l.i2: The option is a dash and the letter “l” (as in “long”).
cr.dev.cp.d: A command that makes a copy of a file.
cr.dev.echo.d: A command that repeats what you tell it.
cr.dev.echo.i1: Its name is the sound that comes back in the mountains.
cr.dev.cd_maison.d: A command that takes me home, in one go.
cr.dev.cd_maison.i1: It's the command that changes folder.
cr.dev.cd_maison.i2: After it comes a little snake: the tilde “~”.
mis.niveau: Next lesson at level {n}: feed me {xp} more XP
ui.lecon.vide: No lesson right now. Explore, feed your creature, or type `aide`.
ui.detail.dit: What the game said after your last command
ui.reg.pur.aide: for older kids: just the terminal, the instruction is written in it
ui.menu.onglets.sous: one more tab, like a 2nd window
ui.pur.on: Pure terminal: just the terminal. The instruction is written in it (➜); ☰ at the top for everything else.
ui.pur.off: Terminal + mission: the 🎯 line is back above the input line.
